tests.title: Ensure Administrative accounts are cloud-only
tests.sum:
1.1.1 (L1) Ensure Administrative accounts are cloud-only

Administrative accounts are special privileged accounts that could have varying levels of access to data, users, and settings. Regular user accounts should never be utilized for administrative tasks and care should be taken, in the case of a hybrid environment, to keep administrative accounts separate from on-prem accounts. Administrative accounts should not have applications assigned so that they have no access to potentially vulnerable services (EX. email, Teams, SharePoint, etc.) and only access to perform tasks as needed for administrative purposes. **Ensure administrative accounts are not On-premises sync enabled.**
tests.fix: Remediation will require first identifying the privileged accounts that are synced from onpremises and then creating a new cloud-only account for that user. Once a replacement account is established, the hybrid account should have its role reduced to that of a nonprivileged user or removed depending on the need.

links.t: Add users and assign licenses in Microsoft 365
Step 2. Protect your Microsoft 365 privileged accounts
9. Use cloud native accounts for Microsoft Entra roles
CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations Benchmark v7.0.0 - Page 21

tests.title: Ensure that between two and four global admins are designated
tests.sum:
1.1.3 (L1) Ensure that between two and four global admins are designated

Between two and four Global Administrators should be designated in the tenant. Ideally, these accounts will not have licenses assigned to them which supports additional controls found in this benchmark.
tests.fix:
Note: If an organization's tenant is using a third-party identity provider, this remediation may not be relevant. The principle of the recommendation is still relevant, and compensating controls that are relevant to the third-party identity provider should be implemented.

To correct the number of global tenant administrators:

1. Navigate to Microsoft 365 admin center [https://admin.microsoft.com](https://admin.microsoft.com).
2. Select **Users** > **Active Users**.
3. In the Search field enter the name of the user to be made a Global Administrator.
4. To create a new Global Administrator:
5. Select the user's name.
6. A window will appear to the right.
7. Select **Manage roles**.
8. Select **Admin center access**.
9. Check **Global Administrator**.
10. Click Save changes.

To remove Global Admins:

1. Select **User**.
2. Under Roles select **Manage roles**.
3. De-Select the appropriate role.
4. Click **Save changes**.

Note: When tallying the number of Global Administrators, Partner relationships (Settings > Partner Relationships) are not accounted for and should be reviewed on a recurring basis.

links.t: 5. Limit the number of Global Administrators to less than 5

tests.title: Ensure that only organizationally managed/approved public groups exist
tests.sum:
1.2.1 (L2) Ensure that only organizationally managed/approved public groups exist

Microsoft 365 Groups is the foundational membership service that drives all teamwork across Microsoft 365. With Microsoft 365 Groups, you can give a group of people access to a collection of shared resources. When a new group is created in the
Administration panel, the default privacy value of the group is "Public". (In this case, ‘public’ means accessible to the identities within the organization without requiring group owner authorization to join.)
Ensure that Microsoft 365 Groups are set to **Private** in the Administration panel.

>Note: Although there are several different group types, this recommendation concerns Microsoft 365 Groups specifically.
tests.fix:
To enable only organizationally managed/approved public groups exist:

1. Navigate to Microsoft 365 admin center [https://admin.microsoft.com](https://admin.microsoft.com).
2. Click to expand **Teams & groups** select **Active teams & groups**.
3. On the **Active teams and groups** page, select the group's name that is public.
4. On the popup groups name page, **Select Settings**.
5. Under Privacy, select **Private**.

>Note: This check only evaluates Microsoft 365 (unified) groups, matching the CIS audit procedure (`groupTypes/any(c:c eq 'Unified')`).

tests.title: Ensure sign-in to shared mailboxes is blocked
tests.sum:
1.2.2 (L1) Ensure sign-in to shared mailboxes is blocked

Shared mailboxes are used when multiple people need access to the same mailbox, such as a company information or support email address, reception desk, or other function that might be shared by multiple people. Users with permissions to the group mailbox can send as or send on behalf of the mailbox email address if the administrator has given that user permissions to do that. This is particularly useful for help and support mailboxes because users can send
emails from "Contoso Support" or "Building A Reception Desk." Shared mailboxes are created with a corresponding user account using a system generated password that is unknown at the time of creation. The recommended state is **Sign in blocked** for **Shared mailboxes**.
tests.fix:
Block sign-in to shared mailboxes in the UI:

1. Navigate to Microsoft 365 admin center [https://admin.microsoft.com](https://admin.microsoft.com).
2. Click to expand **Teams & groups** and select **Shared mailboxes**.
3. Take note of all shared mailboxes.
4. Click to expand **Users** and select **Active users**.
5. Select a shared mailbox account to open its properties pane and then select **Block sign-in**.
6. Check the box for **Block this user from signing in.**
7. Repeat for any additional shared mailboxes.

tests.title: Ensure 'Idle session timeout' is set to '3 hours (or less)' for unmanaged devices
tests.sum:
Browser sessions on unmanaged devices for Microsoft 365 apps end after at most three hours of inactivity.

A browser that someone leaves open on a shared or personal computer keeps the Microsoft 365 session signed in. Anyone who walks up to it, or any malware that runs on it, can use the session. A short idle timeout signs the user out of the web apps when nothing happens for a while.

Two parts are needed: an activity-based timeout policy with a web session idle timeout of 3 hours or less, and a Conditional Access policy that uses **Use app enforced restrictions** for browser access to Office 365 so that the timeout applies to unmanaged devices. The test looks at both.

User and group exclusions are not evaluated by this test. Application exclusions are also not evaluated when the policy targets all apps; verify exclusions are documented and reviewed annually. A condition that narrows …
tests.fix:
1. Sign in to the [Microsoft 365 admin center](https://admin.microsoft.com).
2. Go to **Settings** > **Org settings** > **Security & privacy** > [**Idle session timeout**](https://admin.microsoft.com/#/Settings/SecurityPrivacy/:/Settings/L1/IdleSessionTimeout) and turn it on with a timeout of 3 hours or less.
3. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) and go to **Entra ID** > **Conditional Access** > **Policies**.
4. Create a policy for **All users** and the **Office 365** app, with **Client apps** set to **Browser** only. Under **Session**, select **Use app enforced restrictions** and enable the policy.

tests.title: Ensure Safe Links for Office Applications is Enabled (Only Checks Priority 0 Policy)
tests.sum:
2.1.1 (L2) Ensure Safe Links for Office Applications is Enabled

Enabling Safe Links policy for Office applications allows URL's that exist inside of Office documents and email applications opened by Office, Office Online and Office mobile to be processed against Defender for Office time-of-click verification and rewritten if required.

>Note: E5 Licensing includes a number of Built-in Protection policies. When auditing policies note which policy you are viewing, and keep in mind CIS recommendations often extend the Default or Built-in Policies provided by MS. In order to Pass the highest priority policy must match all settings recommended.
tests.fix:
To create a Safe Links policy:

1. Navigate to Microsoft 365 admin center [https://admin.microsoft.com](https://admin.microsoft.com).
2. Under **Email & collaboration** select **Policies & rules**
3. Select **Threat policies** then **Safe Links**
4. Click on **+Create**
5. Name the policy then click **Next**
6. In **Domains** select all valid domains for the organization and **Next**
7. Ensure the following **URL & click protection settings** are defined:

**Email**

* Checked **On: Safe Links checks a list of known, malicious links when users click links in email. URLs are rewritten by default**
* Checked **Apply Safe Links to email messages sent within the organization**
* Checked **Apply real-time URL scanning for suspicious links and links that point to files**
* Checked **Wait for URL scanning to complete before delivering the message**
* Unchecked **Do not rewrite URLs, do checks via Safe Links API only**.

**Teams**

* Checked **On: Safe Links checks a list of known, malicious links when users click links in Microsoft Teams. URLs are not rewritten**.

**Office 365 Apps**

* Checked On: **Safe Links checks a list of known, malicious links when users click links in Microsoft Office apps. URLs are not rewritten**

**Click protection settings**

* Checked: **Track user clicks**
* Unchecked: **Let users click through the original URL**
* There is no recommendation for organization branding

8. Click **Next** twice and finally **Submit**.

tests.title: Ensure that an anti-phishing policy has been created (Only Checks Default Policy)
tests.sum:
2.1.7 (L1) Ensure that an anti-phishing policy has been created

By default, Office 365 includes built-in features that help protect users from phishing attacks. Set up anti-phishing polices to increase this protection, for example by refining settings to better detect and prevent impersonation and spoofing attacks. The default policy applies to all users within the organization and is a single view to fine-tune antiphishing protection. Custom policies can be created and configured for specific users, groups or domains within the organization and will take precedence over the default policy for the scoped users.
tests.fix:
1. Navigate to [Microsoft 365 Defender](https://security.microsoft.com)
2. Click to expand **Email & collaboration** select **Policies & rules**
3. Select **Threat policies**.
4. Under Policies select **Anti-phishing** and click **Create**.
5. Name the policy, continuing and clicking **Next** as needed:

* Add **Groups** and/or **Domains** that contain a majority of the organization.
* Set **Phishing email threshold** to **3 - More Aggressive**
* Check **Enable users to protect** and add up to 350 users.
* Check **Enable domains to protect** and check **Include domains I own**.
* Check **Enable mailbox intelligence (Recommended)**.
* Check **Enable Intelligence for impersonation protection (Recommended)**.
* Check **Enable spoof intelligence (Recommended)**.

1. Under Actions configure the following:

* Set **If a message is detected as user impersonation to Quarantine the message**.
* Set **If a message is detected as domain impersonation to Quarantine the message**.
* Set **If Mailbox Intelligence detects an impersonated user to Quarantine the message**.
* Leave **Honor DMARC record policy when the message is detected as spoof** checked.
* Check **Show first contact safety tip (Recommended)**.
* Check **Show user impersonation safety tip**.
* Check **Show domain impersonation safety tip**.
* Check **Show user impersonation unusual characters safety tip**.

1. Finally click **Next** and **Submit** the policy.

>Note: DefaultFullAccessWithNotificationPolicy is suggested but not required. Users will be notified that impersonation emails are in the Quarantine

tests.title: Ensure that DKIM is enabled for all Exchange Online Domains
tests.sum:
2.1.9 (L1) Ensure that DKIM is enabled for all Exchange Online Domains

DKIM is one of the trio of Authentication methods (SPF, DKIM and DMARC) that help prevent attackers from sending messages that look like they come from your domain. DKIM lets an organization add a digital signature to outbound email messages in the message header. When DKIM is configured, the organization authorizes it's domain to associate, or sign, its name to an email message using cryptographic authentication. Email systems that get email from this domain can use a digital signature to help verify whether incoming email is legitimate. Use of DKIM in addition to SPF and DMARC to help prevent malicious actors using spoofing techniques from sending messages that look like they are coming from your domain.
tests.fix:
To remediate using a DNS Provider:

1. For each accepted domain in Exchange Online, two DNS entries are required.

```txt
Host name: selector1._domainkey
Points to address or value: selector1-<domainGUID>._domainkey.<initialDomain>
TTL: 3600
Host name: selector2._domainkey
Points to address or value: selector2-<domainGUID>._domainkey.<initialDomain>
TTL: 3600
```

For Office 365, the selectors will always be **selector1** or **selector2**.

domainGUID is the same as the domainGUID in the customized MX record for your custom domain that appears before mail.protection.outlook.com. For example, in the following MX record for the domain contoso.com, the domainGUID is contoso-com:

```txt
contoso.com. 3600 IN MX 5 contoso-com.mail.protection.outlook.com
```

The initial domain is the domain that you used when you signed up for Office 365. Initial domains always end with onmicrosoft.com.

1. After the DNS records are created, enable DKIM signing in Defender.
2. Navigate to [Microsoft 365 Defender](https://security.microsoft.com)
3. Expand **Email & collaboration** > **Policies & rules** > **Threat policies**.
4. Under **Rules** section click **Email authentication settings**.
5. Select **DKIM**
6. Click on each domain and click **Enable** next to **Sign messages for this domain with DKIM signature**.

Final remediation step using the Exchange Online PowerShell Module:

1. Connect to Exchange Online service using `Connect-ExchangeOnline`.
2. Run the following Exchange Online PowerShell command:

```powershell
Set-DkimSigningConfig -Identity < domainName > -Enabled $True
```

tests.title: Ensure the connection filter IP allow list is not used (Only Checks Default Policy)
tests.sum:
2.1.12 (L1) Ensure the connection filter IP allow list is not used

In Microsoft 365 organizations with Exchange Online mailboxes or standalone Exchange Online Protection (EOP) organizations without Exchange Online mailboxes, connection filtering and the default connection filter policy identify good or bad source email servers by IP addresses. The key components of the default connection filter policy are IP Allow List, IP Block List and Safe list.
The recommended state is **IP Allow List** empty or undefined.
tests.fix:
To remove IPs from the allow list:

1. Navigate to [Microsoft 365 Defender](https://security.microsoft.com).
2. Click to expand **Email & collaboration** select **Policies & rules** > **Threat policies**.
3. Under policies select **Anti-spam**.

tests.title: Ensure password addition is blocked for applications
tests.sum:
5.1.5.3 (L2) Ensure password addition is blocked for applications

In Microsoft Entra ID, applications and service principals can authenticate using either certificate credentials or password credentials (also referred to as client secrets). This setting enforces a tenant-wide restriction that prevents new password credentials from being added to any application registration or service principal. The policy is implemented through the default app management policy and applies to all applications unless scoped exceptions are configured.

The setting does not revoke or invalidate existing password credentials; credentials created before the policy was enabled remain valid until they expire or are explicitly removed.

The recommended state is **Block password addition** set to **On**.
tests.fix:
To remediate using the UI:

1. Navigate to [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Expand **Entra ID** and select **Enterprise apps**.
3. Under **Security** select [**Application policies**](https://aka.ms/app-mgmt-policy-ux).
4. Select **Block password addition**.
5. Set **Status** to **On**.
6. Set **Applies to** to one of the following:
    * **All applications**
    * **All applications with exclusions** (if using exclusions, ensure they are reviewed annually).
7. Set **Only apply to apps created after** to a desired date or leave it unconfigured.
8. Select **Save and close** to apply the changes.

To remediate using the Microsoft Graph API:

> **Important:** The PATCH request replaces the `passwordCredentials` array in full. Retrieve the current policy first and include all existing entries in the request body to avoid overwriting other configured restrictions or exclusions.

1. Execute a **GET** request to retrieve the current policy: `v1.0/policies/defaultAppManagementPolicy`
2. Modify the returned JSON to reflect the following changes:
   * Set `isEnabled` to `true`.
   * Under `applicationRestrictions.passwordCredentials`, locate the entry where `restrictionType` is `passwordAddition` and set the following:
      * `state` to `enabled`
      * `restrictForAppsCreatedAfterDateTime` to `0001-01-01T00:00:00Z` or a desired date.
   * Under `servicePrincipalRestrictions.passwordCredentials`, locate the entry where `restrictionType` is `passwordAddition` and set the following:
      * `state` to `enabled`
      * `restrictForAppsCreatedAfterDateTime` to `0001-01-01T00:00:00Z` or a desired date.
3. Execute a **PATCH** request to the same URI with the modified JSON in the request body to apply the changes.

> **Note:** Maester also checks that the restriction covers every existing application and service principal. Objects created before the **Only apply to apps created after** date (`restrictForAppsCreatedAfterDateTime`) are exempt from the restriction, so the check fails while any exist. Leave the date unconfigured or set it to `0001-01-01T00:00:00Z`, or to a date before your oldest application and service principal.

tests.title: Ensure password lifetime for applications does not exceed 180 days
tests.sum:

This setting enforces a tenant-wide maximum lifetime for new password credentials added to any application registration or service principal. When enabled, any client secret created must have an expiration date that falls within the configured maximum, which for this recommendation is 180 days or less. The policy is implemented through the default app management policy and applies to all applications unless scoped exceptions are configured.

The setting does not retroactively shorten or invalidate existing password credentials; secrets created before the policy was enabled remain valid until they expire or are explicitly removed.

The recommended state is **Restrict …

To remediate using the UI:

1. Navigate to [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Expand **Entra ID** and select **Enterprise apps**.
3. Under **Security** select [**Application policies**](https://aka.ms/app-mgmt-policy-ux).
4. Select **Restrict max password lifetime**.
5. Set **Status** to **On**.
6. Set the maximum lifetime to **180** days or less.
7. Set **Applies to** to one of the following:

    * **All applications with exclusions** (if using exclusions, ensure they are reviewed annually).

> **Important:** The PATCH request replaces the `passwordCredentials` array in full. Retrieve the current policy first and include all existing entries in the request body to avoid overwriting other configured restrictions or exclusions.

2. Modify the returned JSON to reflect the following changes:
   * Set `isEnabled` to `true`.
   * Under `applicationRestrictions.passwordCredentials`, locate the entry where `restrictionType` is `passwordLifetime` and set the following:
      * `state` to `enabled`

      * `state` to `enabled`
      * `maxLifetime` to `P180D` or a shorter duration.
      * `restrictForAppsCreatedAfterDateTime` to `0001-01-01T00:00:00Z` or a desired date.
3. Execute a **PATCH** request to the same URI with the modified JSON in the request body to apply the changes.

> **Note:** Maester also checks that the restriction covers every existing application and service principal. Objects created before the **Only apply to apps created after** date (`restrictForAppsCreatedAfterDateTime`) are exempt from the restriction, so the check fails while any exist. Leave the date unconfigured or set it to `0001-01-01T00:00:00Z`, or to a date before your oldest application and service principal.

> **Note:** Maester also checks that the restriction covers every existing application and service principal. Objects created before the **Only apply to apps created after** date (`restrictForAppsCreatedAfterDateTime`) are exempt from the restriction, so the check fails while any exist. Leave the date unconfigured or set it to `0001-01-01T00:00:00Z`, or to a date before your oldest application and service principal.

tests.title: Ensure that collaboration invitations are sent to allowed domains only
tests.sum:
5.1.6.1 (L2) Ensure that collaboration invitations are sent to allowed domains only

B2B collaboration is a feature within Microsoft Entra External ID that allows for guest invitations to an organization.

Ensure users can only send invitations to **specified domains**.

This check evaluates every B2B management policy returned by Microsoft Graph, not only the organization default. It does not inspect which applications or service principals are assigned each policy.

> **Note:** This list works independently from OneDrive for Business and SharePoint Online allow/block lists. To restrict individual file sharing in SharePoint Online, set up an allow or blocklist for OneDrive for Business and SharePoint Online. For instance, in SharePoint or OneDrive users can still share with external users from prohibited domains by using Anyone links if they haven't been disabled.
tests.fix:
To remediate using the UI:

1. Navigate to Microsoft Entra admin center [https://entra.microsoft.com](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Expand **Entra ID** > **External Identities** and select **External collaboration settings**.
3. Under **Collaboration restrictions**, select **Allow invitations only to the specified domains (most restrictive)**.
4. Specify the allowed domains under **Target domains**.
5. Select **Save**.

> **Note:** The default value is **Allow invitations to be sent to any domain (most inclusive)**. A configuration with a list of blocked domains (**Deny invitations to the specified domains**) is not compliant.

tests.title: Ensure that guest user access is restricted
tests.sum:
5.1.6.2 (L1) Ensure that guest user access is restricted

Microsoft Entra ID, part of Microsoft Entra, allows you to restrict what external guest users can see in their organization in Microsoft Entra ID. Guest users are set to a limited permission level by default in Microsoft Entra ID, while the default for member users is the full set of user permissions.

These directory level permissions are enforced across Microsoft Entra services including Microsoft Graph, PowerShell v2, the Azure portal, and My Apps portal. Microsoft 365 services leveraging Microsoft 365 groups for collaboration scenarios are also affected, specifically Outlook, Microsoft Teams, and SharePoint. They do not override the SharePoint or Microsoft Teams guest settings.

The recommended state is at least **Guest users have limited access to properties and memberships of directory objects** or more restrictive.
tests.fix:
1. Navigate to [Microsoft Entra ID admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Click to expand **Entra ID** > **External Identities** select **External collaboration settings**.
3. Under **Guest user access** set **Guest user access restrictions** to one of the following:

* State: **Guest users have limited access to properties and memberships of directory objects**
* State: **Guest user access is restricted to properties and memberships of their own directory objects (most restrictive)**

tests.title: Ensure guest user invitations are limited
tests.sum:
5.1.6.3 (L2) Ensure guest user invitations are limited

By default, all users in the organization, including B2B collaboration guest users, can invite external users to B2B collaboration. The ability to send invitations can be limited by turning it on or off for everyone, or by restricting invitations to certain roles.

The recommended state is **Only users assigned to specific admin roles can invite guest users** or **No one in the organization can invite guest users including admins (most restrictive)**.
tests.fix:
To remediate using the UI:

1. Navigate to Microsoft Entra admin center [https://entra.microsoft.com](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Expand **Entra ID** > **External Identities** and select **External collaboration settings**.
3. Under **Guest invite settings** set **Guest invite restrictions** to one of the following:
   - **Only users assigned to specific admin roles can invite guest users**
   - **No one in the organization can invite guest users including admins (most restrictive)**
4. Select **Save**.

tests.title: Ensure that password hash sync is enabled for hybrid deployments
tests.sum:
5.1.8.1 (L1) Ensure that password hash sync is enabled for hybrid deployments

Password Hash Synchronization is one of the sign-in methods used to enable hybrid identity authentication. With this method, Microsoft Entra Connect synchronizes a cryptographically derived representation of a user's on-premises Active Directory password to Microsoft Entra ID.

The original NT password hash (MD4) is never transmitted to Entra ID. Instead, Entra Connect computes a SHA-256 hash of the original MD4 hash and synchronizes that value. Because only this secondary hash is stored in the cloud, the credential material in Entra ID cannot be reused for on-premises pass-the-hash attacks, even if compromised.

> **Note:** This recommendation applies only to Microsoft 365 tenants operating in a hybrid identity configuration using Microsoft Entra Connect. It does not apply to federated or cloud-only …
tests.fix:
To remediate using the on-premises Microsoft Entra Connect tool:

1. Log in to the on-premises server that hosts the Microsoft Entra Connect tool.
2. Double-click the **Azure AD Connect** icon that was created on the desktop.
3. Click **Configure**.
4. On the **Additional tasks** page, select **Customize synchronization options** and click **Next**.
5. Enter the username and password for your global administrator.
6. On the **Connect your directories** screen, click **Next**.
7. On the **Domain and OU filtering** screen, click **Next**.
8. On the **Optional features** screen, check **Password hash synchronization** and click **Next**.
9. On the **Ready to configure** screen, click **Configure**.
10. Once the configuration completes, click **Exit**.

> **Note:** Microsoft Entra Connect sync is disabled by default. Password Hash Sync is Microsoft's recommended setting for new deployments.

tests.title: Ensure multifactor authentication is enabled for all users in administrative roles
tests.sum:
An enabled Conditional Access policy requires multifactor authentication for the privileged directory roles, in all cloud apps.

Administrator accounts can change identity, mail and security configuration for the whole organisation. A password alone is enough for an attacker who phished or sprayed it. Requiring MFA at sign-in for these roles makes a stolen password insufficient.

The test passes when one enabled policy lists every role in the set that the test checks: Application, Authentication, Billing, Cloud Application, Conditional Access, Exchange, Global, Helpdesk, Password, Privileged Authentication, Privileged Role, Security, SharePoint and User Administrator roles, plus Global Reader. Policies in report-only mode do not count. Keep emergency access accounts in the policy exclusions.

User and group exclusions are not evaluated by this test. Application exclusions are also not …
tests.fix:
1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Go to **Entra ID** > **Conditional Access** > [**Policies**](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_ConditionalAccess/ConditionalAccessBlade/~/Policies) and select **New policy**.
3. Under **Users**, select **Include** > **Select users and groups** > **Directory roles** and add every role listed above. Exclude your emergency access accounts.
4. Under **Target resources**, select **All resources (formerly All cloud apps)**.
5. Under **Grant**, select **Grant access** and **Require multifactor authentication** (or **Require authentication strength**).
6. Set **Enable policy** to **On** (use **Report-only** first to measure the impact) and select **Create**.

tests.title: Ensure multifactor authentication is enabled for all users
tests.sum:
An enabled Conditional Access policy requires multifactor authentication for all users, in all cloud apps.

Passwords are the most common way into Microsoft 365 accounts: they are phished, reused, guessed and sprayed. Requiring a second factor for every user at sign-in blocks most of these attacks even when the password is known.

The policy must target all users and all resources, require MFA or an authentication strength, and be enabled. Policies that apply only at a certain risk level, or that are in report-only mode, do not satisfy the test. Excluding emergency access accounts is expected.

User and group exclusions are not evaluated by this test. Application exclusions are also not evaluated when the policy targets all apps; verify exclusions are documented and reviewed annually. A condition that narrows the policy is reported unless the check is about that condition.
tests.fix:
1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Go to **Entra ID** > **Conditional Access** > [**Policies**](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_ConditionalAccess/ConditionalAccessBlade/~/Policies) and select **New policy**.
3. Under **Users**, include **All users**. Exclude your emergency access accounts.
4. Under **Target resources**, select **All resources (formerly All cloud apps)**.
5. Under **Grant**, select **Grant access** and **Require multifactor authentication** (or **Require authentication strength**).
6. Set **Enable policy** to **On** (use **Report-only** first to measure the impact) and select **Create**.

tests.title: Enable Conditional Access policies to block legacy authentication
tests.sum:
An enabled Conditional Access policy blocks sign-ins from legacy authentication clients for all users.

Legacy authentication protocols such as POP, IMAP, SMTP AUTH and older Office clients do not support multifactor authentication. An attacker who has a password can use them to sign in without the MFA prompt, and password spray tools target them first.

The policy must apply to all users and all cloud apps, select both **Exchange ActiveSync clients** and **Other clients**, block access and be enabled. Check the sign-in logs for legacy usage first, because blocking breaks applications that still depend on these protocols.

User and group exclusions are not evaluated by this test. Application exclusions are also not evaluated when the policy targets all apps; verify exclusions are documented and reviewed annually. A condition that narrows the policy is reported unless the check is about …
tests.fix:
1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Go to **Entra ID** > **Conditional Access** > [**Policies**](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_ConditionalAccess/ConditionalAccessBlade/~/Policies) and select **New policy**.
3. Under **Users**, include **All users**. Exclude your emergency access accounts.
4. Under **Target resources**, select **All resources (formerly All cloud apps)**.
5. Under **Conditions** > **Client apps**, set **Configure** to **Yes** and select **Exchange ActiveSync clients** and **Other clients** only.
6. Under **Grant**, select **Block access**.
7. Set **Enable policy** to **On** (use **Report-only** first to measure the impact) and select **Create**.

tests.title: Ensure Sign-in frequency is enabled and browser sessions are not persistent for Administrative users
tests.sum:
An enabled Conditional Access policy sets a short sign-in frequency and turns off persistent browser sessions for the administrative roles.

A session token that stays valid for days or survives a browser restart can be stolen and replayed on another machine. Administrators hold the most valuable sessions, so shortening how long a session lasts, and not keeping it after the browser closes, limits how long a stolen token is useful.

The policy must apply to the same set of administrative roles as the MFA test, cover all cloud apps, set a sign-in frequency of 4 hours or less (or every time), set persistent browser session to **Never persistent** and be enabled.

User and group exclusions are not evaluated by this test. Application exclusions are also not evaluated when the policy targets all apps; verify exclusions are documented and reviewed annually. A condition that narrows the policy …
tests.fix:
1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Go to **Entra ID** > **Conditional Access** > [**Policies**](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_ConditionalAccess/ConditionalAccessBlade/~/Policies) and select **New policy**.
3. Under **Users**, select **Directory roles** and add the administrative roles. Exclude your emergency access accounts.
4. Under **Target resources**, select **All resources (formerly All cloud apps)**.
5. Under **Session**, select **Sign-in frequency** and set it to **Periodic reauthentication** of 4 hours or less, or **Every time**.
6. Under **Session**, select **Persistent browser session** and choose **Never persistent**.
7. Set **Enable policy** to **On** (use **Report-only** first to measure the impact) and select **Create**.

tests.title: Ensure 'Phishing-resistant MFA strength' is required for Administrators
tests.sum:
An enabled Conditional Access policy requires the phishing-resistant MFA authentication strength for the administrative roles.

Push notifications, SMS and one-time codes can be relayed by an adversary-in-the-middle phishing site. Phishing-resistant methods bind the sign-in to the real site, so a relayed prompt does not work. Administrators are the highest-value targets, so they are the first accounts to move to these methods.

Users need a registered FIDO2 security key, Windows Hello for Business or a certificate before the policy is enabled for them, otherwise they are locked out. Roll out in report-only mode and keep emergency access accounts excluded.

The allowed combinations must be a non-empty subset of Windows Hello for Business, FIDO2 or certificate-based multifactor authentication. It does not need to include all three, and any other method makes the check fail.

Policies with …

tests.title: Enable Identity Protection user risk policies
tests.sum:
An enabled Conditional Access policy responds to high user risk by requiring MFA and a password change, with sign-in frequency set to every time.

Microsoft Entra ID Protection marks an account as high risk when it has strong evidence that the credentials are leaked or the account is compromised. A policy that forces MFA and a password change lets the legitimate user recover automatically and gives the attacker nothing to reuse.

The policy needs Microsoft Entra ID P2 licences. Policies that also select medium or low risk are accepted, as long as high is included.

User and group exclusions are not evaluated by this test. Application exclusions are also not evaluated when the policy targets all apps; verify exclusions are documented and reviewed annually. A condition that narrows the policy is reported unless the check is about that condition.
tests.fix:
1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Go to **Entra ID** > **Conditional Access** > [**Policies**](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_ConditionalAccess/ConditionalAccessBlade/~/Policies) and select **New policy**.

4. Under **Target resources**, select **All resources (formerly All cloud apps)**.

8. Set **Enable policy** to **On** (use **Report-only** first to measure the impact) and select **Create**.

tests.title: Enable Identity Protection sign-in risk policies
tests.sum:
An enabled Conditional Access policy responds to medium and high sign-in risk by requiring MFA every time or by blocking access.

Microsoft Entra ID Protection scores each sign-in on how likely it is that someone other than the account owner started it, for example an anonymous IP address, impossible travel or a leaked-credential match. A policy that responds to the score challenges or stops suspicious sign-ins even when the password is correct.

The policy needs Microsoft Entra ID P2 licences. Both medium and high must be selected. A policy that blocks access at those levels is stricter and is accepted.

User and group exclusions are not evaluated by this test. Application exclusions are also not evaluated when the policy targets all apps; verify exclusions are documented and reviewed annually. A condition that narrows the policy is reported unless the check is about that condition.

tests.title: Ensure 'sign-in risk' is blocked for medium and high risk
tests.sum:
An enabled Conditional Access policy blocks access when the sign-in risk is medium or high.

Asking a risky sign-in for MFA still leaves the account open to an attacker who can complete the prompt, for example by relaying it. Blocking sign-ins that Microsoft Entra ID Protection rates medium or high stops them before a session exists, and users with a genuine need are sent to the helpdesk.

The policy needs Microsoft Entra ID P2 licences. Expect some false positives, so involve the helpdesk before enabling it.

User and group exclusions are not evaluated by this test. Application exclusions are also not evaluated when the policy targets all apps; verify exclusions are documented and reviewed annually. A condition that narrows the policy is reported unless the check is about that condition.

tests.title: Ensure a managed device is required for authentication
tests.sum:
An enabled Conditional Access policy requires a compliant device (or, as an alternative, a hybrid joined device) for all users and all cloud apps.

A stolen password or session token is far less useful when sign-in is limited to devices that your organisation manages and that meet its security baseline. Unmanaged devices are the usual source of malware that steals tokens.

This is a high-impact control: personal and partner devices lose access unless you provide an alternative such as browser-only access with session controls. Enrol devices in Microsoft Intune and define compliance policies before enabling the policy, and use report-only mode first.

User and group exclusions are not evaluated by this test. Application exclusions are also not evaluated when the policy targets all apps; verify exclusions are documented and reviewed annually. A condition that narrows the policy is …
tests.fix:
1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).

6. Set **Enable policy** to **On** (use **Report-only** first to measure the impact) and select **Create**.

tests.title: Ensure a managed device is required to register security information
tests.sum:
An enabled Conditional Access policy requires a compliant device (or, as an alternative, a hybrid joined device) when users register or change their security information.

An attacker who has a password and can register their own authentication method controls the account from then on. Limiting registration to managed devices stops that persistence step from an unmanaged machine.

The policy applies to the register security information user action rather than to apps. Users who need to register from a new device can use a temporary access pass from a managed device or the office network.

User and group exclusions are not evaluated by this test. Application exclusions are also not evaluated when the policy targets all apps; verify exclusions are documented and reviewed annually. A condition that narrows the policy is reported unless the check is about that condition.
tests.fix:
1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Go to **Entra ID** > **Conditional Access** > [**Policies**](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_ConditionalAccess/ConditionalAccessBlade/~/Policies) and select **New policy**.

tests.title: Ensure sign-in frequency for Intune Enrollment is set to 'Every time'
tests.sum:
An enabled Conditional Access policy requires MFA every time a user enrols a device in Microsoft Intune.

Enrolling a device gives it a managed identity that other Conditional Access policies trust. If an attacker enrols a device with a stolen session, that device then satisfies the managed device requirements. Asking for a fresh MFA on every enrolment keeps the enrolment step tied to the real user.

The policy targets the Microsoft Intune Enrollment cloud app, which appears in the app picker once Intune is licensed.

User and group exclusions are not evaluated by this test. Application exclusions are also not evaluated when the policy targets all apps; verify exclusions are documented and reviewed annually. A condition that narrows the policy is reported unless the check is about that condition.
tests.fix:
1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Go to **Entra ID** > **Conditional Access** > [**Policies**](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_ConditionalAccess/ConditionalAccessBlade/~/Policies) and select **New policy**.
3. Under **Users**, include **All users**. Exclude your emergency access accounts.
4. Under **Target resources**, select **Select resources** and add **Microsoft Intune Enrollment**.
5. Under **Grant**, select **Grant access** and **Require multifactor authentication**.
6. Under **Session**, select **Sign-in frequency** and set it to **Every time**.
7. Set **Enable policy** to **On** (use **Report-only** first to measure the impact) and select **Create**.

tests.title: Ensure the device code sign-in flow is blocked
tests.sum:
An enabled Conditional Access policy blocks the device code authentication flow for all users and all cloud apps.

In device code phishing, an attacker starts a device code sign-in and tricks the victim into entering the code on the genuine Microsoft sign-in page. The victim completes MFA and the attacker receives valid tokens. The flow exists for devices without a keyboard, which most organisations do not use.

Blocking the flow removes the technique. A device filter or an excluded role other than the two directory synchronization roles is reported by this check. User and group exclusions are not evaluated, and application exclusions are not evaluated when the policy targets all apps; document and review such exclusions separately.
tests.fix:
1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Go to **Entra ID** > **Conditional Access** > [**Policies**](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_ConditionalAccess/ConditionalAccessBlade/~/Policies) and select **New policy**.
3. Under **Users**, include **All users**. Exclude your emergency access accounts.
4. Under **Target resources**, select **All resources (formerly All cloud apps)**.
5. Under **Conditions** > **Authentication flows**, set **Configure** to **Yes** and select **Device code flow**.
6. Under **Grant**, select **Block access**.
7. Set **Enable policy** to **On** (use **Report-only** first to measure the impact) and select **Create**.

Block authentication flows with Conditional Access

tests.title: Ensure that periodic reauthentication is required for all users
tests.sum:
An enabled Conditional Access policy requires all users to sign in again after at most seven days.

Without a limit, a session can stay valid for a very long time, and a refresh token that is stolen keeps working until the user next changes password. Periodic reauthentication forces a new sign-in, and a new MFA challenge, at a predictable interval, which caps how long a stolen session is useful.

The policy must apply to all users and all cloud apps, set the frequency to 7 days or less (or every time) and be enabled. Short intervals add prompts for users, so pick the longest interval that your risk appetite allows.

User and group exclusions are not evaluated by this test. Application exclusions are also not evaluated when the policy targets all apps; verify exclusions are documented and reviewed annually. A condition that narrows the policy is reported unless the check is about that …
tests.fix:
1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Go to **Entra ID** > **Conditional Access** > [**Policies**](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_ConditionalAccess/ConditionalAccessBlade/~/Policies) and select **New policy**.
3. Under **Users**, include **All users**. Exclude your emergency access accounts.
4. Under **Target resources**, select **All resources (formerly All cloud apps)**.
5. Under **Session**, select **Sign-in frequency**, choose **Periodic reauthentication** and enter 7 days or less (or choose **Every time**).
6. Set **Enable policy** to **On** (use **Report-only** first to measure the impact) and select **Create**.

links.t: Microsoft Entra admin center - Conditional Access policies

tests.title: Ensure trusted 'named locations' are defined
tests.sum:
At least one IP-based named location with address ranges exists and is marked as trusted.

Named locations give Conditional Access a way to tell your offices and known egress addresses from the rest of the internet. Marked as trusted, they feed Microsoft Entra ID Protection and let policies relax or tighten requirements by network.

The test passes when at least one IP named location has ranges and is trusted. Country-based locations are not counted. Only mark a network as trusted when it is under your control.
tests.fix:
1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Go to **Entra ID** > **Conditional Access** > [**Named locations**](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_ConditionalAccess/ConditionalAccessBlade/~/NamedLocations).
3. Select **IP ranges location**.
4. Enter a name and add the public IP ranges of your offices or egress points.
5. Select **Mark as trusted location** and then **Create**.

links.t: Microsoft Entra admin center - Named locations

tests.title: Ensure exclusionary geographic access controls are utilized
tests.sum:
An enabled Conditional Access policy blocks access from selected untrusted locations and excludes at least one trusted location.

Most organisations know where their staff sign in from. A policy that blocks all locations except the trusted ones, or the countries you operate in, stops a large share of credential attacks that come from elsewhere without any extra step for users.

The policy must apply to all users and all cloud apps, block access and be enabled. It must include all locations or only untrusted locations (countries, or IP ranges not marked as trusted), and exclude **All trusted networks and locations** or at least one trusted IP location. Without a trusted-location exclusion, a block policy could block every sign-in. Plan for travelling users, for example with a temporary exclusion group, and remember that attackers can use VPNs in allowed countries, so this does not …
tests.fix:
1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Make sure your trusted locations exist in [Named locations](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_ConditionalAccess/ConditionalAccessBlade/~/NamedLocations) and are marked as trusted.
3. Go to **Entra ID** > **Conditional Access** > [**Policies**](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_ConditionalAccess/ConditionalAccessBlade/~/Policies) and select **New policy**.
4. Under **Users**, include **All users**. Exclude your emergency access accounts.
5. Under **Target resources**, select **All resources (formerly All cloud apps)**.
6. Under **Conditions** > **Locations**, set **Configure** to **Yes**, include **Any network or location** and exclude your trusted locations (or **All trusted networks and locations**). To block only the countries you list, select those countries under include instead.
7. Under **Grant**, select **Block access**.
8. Set **Enable policy** to **On** (use **Report-only** first to measure the impact) and select **Create**.

Block access by location with Conditional Access

tests.title: Ensure Token Protection is enforced for session tokens
tests.sum:
An enabled Conditional Access policy requires token protection for Exchange Online, SharePoint Online and Microsoft Teams on Windows desktop clients.

Session tokens are bearer tokens: whoever holds one can use it. Token protection binds a sign-in token to the device it was issued to, so a token copied by malware or a proxy does not work from another machine.

The capability is limited to supported Windows clients and to Exchange Online, SharePoint Online and Teams, and incompatible apps are blocked. The benchmark requires a user scope other than **None**. Check the sign-in logs in report-only mode to see which users and apps would be affected before enforcing.

User and group exclusions are not evaluated by this test. Application exclusions are also not evaluated when the policy targets all apps; verify exclusions are documented and reviewed annually. A condition that narrows the …
tests.fix:
1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Go to **Entra ID** > **Conditional Access** > [**Policies**](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_ConditionalAccess/ConditionalAccessBlade/~/Policies) and select **New policy**.
3. Under **Users**, include a non-empty user scope; the benchmark requires this field to be other than **None**.
4. Under **Target resources**, select **Select resources** and add **Office 365 Exchange Online**, **Office 365 SharePoint Online** and **Microsoft Teams Services**.
5. Under **Conditions** > **Device platforms**, include **Windows**. Under **Client apps**, select **Mobile apps and desktop clients** only.
6. Under **Session**, select **Require token protection for sign-in sessions**.
7. Set **Enable policy** to **On** (use **Report-only** first to measure the impact) and select **Create**.

links.t: Microsoft Entra admin center - Conditional Access policies

tests.title: Ensure authentication transfer is blocked
tests.sum:
An enabled Conditional Access policy blocks the authentication transfer flow for all users and all cloud apps.

Authentication transfer lets a signed-in session on one device start a session on another device, for example from a desktop browser to a mobile app. The second device inherits the trust of the first without its own sign-in, which attackers can abuse by getting a victim to scan a QR code.

Blocking the flow forces every device to sign in on its own and so to meet its own Conditional Access requirements.

User and group exclusions are not evaluated by this test. Application exclusions are also not evaluated when the policy targets all apps; verify exclusions are documented and reviewed annually. A condition that narrows the policy is reported unless the check is about that condition.
tests.fix:
1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Go to **Entra ID** > **Conditional Access** > [**Policies**](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_ConditionalAccess/ConditionalAccessBlade/~/Policies) and select **New policy**.
3. Under **Users**, include **All users**. Exclude your emergency access accounts.
4. Under **Target resources**, select **All resources (formerly All cloud apps)**.
5. Under **Conditions** > **Authentication flows**, set **Configure** to **Yes** and select **Authentication transfer**.
6. Under **Grant**, select **Block access**.
7. Set **Enable policy** to **On** (use **Report-only** first to measure the impact) and select **Create**.

links.t: Microsoft Entra admin center - Conditional Access policies
Block authentication flows with Conditional Access

tests.title: Ensure Microsoft Authenticator is configured to protect against MFA fatigue
tests.sum:
Microsoft Authenticator is enabled for all users and its push notifications show the application name and the geographic location of the sign-in request.

In an MFA fatigue attack, an attacker who has a user's password triggers repeated push prompts until the user approves one. Showing which application is signing in and from where gives the user the information needed to recognise and deny a request they did not start.

The change affects the Authenticator prompt only. Users see extra context, and number matching stays in place.
tests.fix:
1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Go to **Entra ID** > **Authentication methods** > [**Policies**](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_IAM/AuthenticationMethodsMenuBlade/~/AdminAuthMethods).
3. Select **Microsoft Authenticator**, set **Enable** to on and target **All users**.
4. On the **Configure** tab, set **Show application name in push and passwordless notifications** to **Enabled** and target **All users**.
5. Set **Show geographic location in push and passwordless notifications** to **Enabled** and target **All users**.
6. Select **Save**.

tests.title: Ensure custom banned passwords lists are used
tests.sum:
The custom banned password list in Microsoft Entra password protection is enabled and contains at least one word.

Password spray attacks try a small number of likely passwords against many accounts. Global banned passwords cover common choices, but words that are specific to your organisation, such as brand names, product names, locations and project names, are not covered unless you add them to the custom list.

The custom list is checked when a user changes or resets a password. Existing passwords are not affected until they change.
tests.fix:
1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Go to **Entra ID** > **Authentication methods** > [**Password protection**](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_IAM/AuthenticationMethodsMenuBlade/~/PasswordProtection).
3. Set **Enforce custom list** to **Yes**.
4. Enter the words to block in **Custom banned password list**, one per line.
5. Select **Save**.

links.t: Microsoft Entra admin center - Password protection
Eliminate bad passwords using Microsoft Entra Password Protection

tests.title: Ensure password protection is enabled for on-prem Active Directory
tests.sum:
Microsoft Entra password protection is enabled for on-premises Active Directory and runs in enforced mode.

Hybrid environments allow password changes against domain controllers. Without the on-premises integration, those changes bypass the banned password lists, so users can set passwords that the cloud would reject. Password spraying tries a few common passwords against many accounts, and the banned password list is what stops those passwords from being set. In audit mode, banned passwords are only logged and are still accepted.

The setting does not take effect until the password protection proxy service and the domain controller agent are installed. If your tenant has no on-premises Active Directory, this recommendation does not apply.
tests.fix:
1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Go to **Entra ID** > **Authentication methods** > [**Password protection**](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_IAM/AuthenticationMethodsMenuBlade/~/PasswordProtection).
3. Set **Enable password protection on Windows Server Active Directory** to **Yes**.
4. Set **Mode** to **Enforced**. Use **Audit** first if you want to measure impact before enforcing.
5. Select **Save**.
6. Install the Microsoft Entra password protection proxy and domain controller agent on-premises if they are not deployed yet.

links.t: Microsoft Entra admin center - Password protection
Plan and deploy on-premises Microsoft Entra Password Protection
Enforce on-premises Microsoft Entra Password Protection

tests.title: Ensure all member users are 'MFA capable'
tests.sum:
Every member user has registered at least one authentication method that can satisfy multifactor authentication.

A Conditional Access policy that requires MFA only helps if users can complete it. A user who has not registered a usable method is either locked out when the policy is enforced or is excluded from it, and in both cases the account is protected by a password alone.

The test reads the registration report, which can lag behind recent changes by a short time. Accounts that are not used for interactive sign-in should be reviewed and, if no longer needed, disabled or removed.
tests.fix:
1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Go to **Entra ID** > **Authentication methods** > [**User registration details**](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_IAM/AuthenticationMethodsMenuBlade/~/UserRegistrationDetails).
3. Filter on **Is MFA capable** = **No** and **User type** = **Member**.
4. Ask each listed user to register a method at [https://aka.ms/mysecurityinfo](https://aka.ms/mysecurityinfo), or enable a registration campaign or a Conditional Access policy for the security information registration user action.
5. Disable or delete accounts that are no longer in use.

tests.title: Ensure weak authentication methods are disabled
tests.sum:
5.2.3.5 (L1) Ensure weak authentication methods are disabled

Authentication methods support a wide variety of scenarios for signing in to Microsoft 365 resources. Some of these methods are inherently more secure than others but require more investment in time to get users enrolled and operational.

SMS and Voice Call rely on telephony carrier communication methods to deliver the authenticating factor.

The recommended state is to Disable these methods:

* SMS
* Voice Call
tests.fix:
1. Navigate to [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Click to expand **Entra ID** > **Authentication methods**
3. Select **Policies**.
4. Inspect each method that is out of compliance and remediate:

* Click on the method to open it.
* Change the **Enable** toggle to the off position.
* Click **Save**.

>Note: If the save button remains greyed out after toggling a method off, then first turn it back on and then change the position of the Target selection (all users or select groups). Turn the method off again and save. This was observed to be a bug in the UI at the time this document was published.

What is SIM swapping & how does the hijacking scam work?
CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations Benchmark v7.0.0 - Page 363

tests.title: Ensure system-preferred multifactor authentication is enabled
tests.sum:
System-preferred multifactor authentication is enabled and applies to all users.

With the feature on, Microsoft Entra ID prompts for the most secure method the user has registered and that is allowed, rather than the method the user picked last or a weaker default. Users who registered both an authenticator app and SMS are asked to use the app, which resists interception and phishing better.

Users can still choose another method from the prompt. The setting only changes which method is offered first.
tests.fix:
1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Go to **Entra ID** > **Authentication methods** > [**Settings**](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_IAM/AuthenticationMethodsMenuBlade/~/AdminAuthMethods).
3. Set **System-preferred multifactor authentication** to **Enabled**.
4. Set the target to **All users**.
5. Select **Save**.

links.t: Microsoft Entra admin center - Authentication methods policies

tests.title: Ensure the email OTP authentication method is disabled
tests.sum:
The email one-time passcode (Email OTP) authentication method is disabled in the Microsoft Entra authentication methods policy.

Email OTP sends a passcode to an email address, and Microsoft Entra uses it to sign in B2B guest users who cannot authenticate with another method. Whoever controls or intercepts that inbox can sign in as the guest, and the inbox of an external user is outside your control. A phished or compromised mailbox then gives access to the resources the guest can reach.

Disabling the method means unverified guests can no longer redeem invitations with an emailed passcode. They must use a Microsoft account, a Microsoft Entra account, a federated identity provider or a social identity provider, or be configured as a guest in your tenant.
tests.fix:
1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Go to **Entra ID** > **Authentication methods** > [**Policies**](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_IAM/AuthenticationMethodsMenuBlade/~/AdminAuthMethods).
3. Select **Email OTP**.
4. Set **Enable** to off.
5. Select **Save**.

To disable the method with PowerShell, connect with `Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'Policy.ReadWrite.AuthenticationMethod'` and run:

```powershell
$params = @{
    '@odata.type' = '#microsoft.graph.emailAuthenticationMethodConfiguration'
    state = 'disabled'
}
Update-MgPolicyAuthenticationMethodPolicyAuthenticationMethodConfiguration -AuthenticationMethodConfigurationId 'Email' -BodyParameter $params
```

tests.title: Ensure that Account 'Lockout threshold' is '10' or less
tests.sum:
The smart lockout threshold does not exceed the recommended maximum of failed sign-in attempts.

Smart lockout slows password guessing and spraying by locking an account out after a number of failed sign-ins. A high threshold gives an attacker more guesses per lockout period.

When the threshold is not stored in the tenant's password rule settings, Microsoft Entra applies its default of 10 failed attempts in public cloud tenants, which meets the recommendation. Lockout duration is checked by a separate test.
tests.fix:
1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Go to **Entra ID** > **Authentication methods** > [**Password protection**](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_IAM/AuthenticationMethodsMenuBlade/~/PasswordProtection).
3. Set **Lockout threshold** to 10 or less.
4. Select **Save**.

links.t: Microsoft Entra admin center - Password protection
Protect user accounts from attacks with Microsoft Entra smart lockout

tests.title: Ensure that Account 'Lockout duration in seconds' is at least 60 seconds
tests.sum:
The smart lockout duration is not shorter than the recommended minimum.

When smart lockout triggers, the account is locked for the configured duration. A very short duration lets an attacker resume guessing almost immediately, which cancels the benefit of the threshold.

When the duration is not stored in the tenant's password rule settings, Microsoft Entra applies its default of 60 seconds, which meets the recommendation. Lockout threshold is checked by a separate test.
tests.fix:
1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Go to **Entra ID** > **Authentication methods** > [**Password protection**](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_IAM/AuthenticationMethodsMenuBlade/~/PasswordProtection).
3. Set **Lockout duration in seconds** to 60 or more.
4. Select **Save**.

links.t: Microsoft Entra admin center - Password protection
Protect user accounts from attacks with Microsoft Entra smart lockout

tests.title: Ensure Microsoft Authenticator on companion applications is disabled
tests.sum:
Microsoft Authenticator functionality on companion applications, such as Outlook, is disabled.

When this feature is on, a user can approve a sign-in request from within a companion app on the same phone that is used to sign in. Approving on the device that started the request weakens the separation between the first factor and the second factor, and a compromised app or device can then complete both.

Disabling it means approvals are given only in the Microsoft Authenticator app itself.
tests.fix:
1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Go to **Entra ID** > **Authentication methods** > [**Policies**](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_IAM/AuthenticationMethodsMenuBlade/~/AdminAuthMethods).
3. Select **Microsoft Authenticator** and open the **Configure** tab.
4. Set **Microsoft Authenticator on companion applications** to **Disabled**.
5. Select **Save**.

links.t: Microsoft Entra admin center - Authentication methods policies
Enable Microsoft Authenticator on companion applications

tests.title: Ensure privileged role assignments are activated and not assigned
tests.sum:
Privileged directory roles are held through Privileged Identity Management (PIM) activation instead of permanent active assignment.

An account with a permanent privileged role is a permanent target: a stolen password or token gives immediate administrative access, at any hour, with no approval, justification or time limit. Making the role eligible means the account is an ordinary user until an admin activates the role for a few hours, with MFA and an audit trail. An attacker who adds a role to an account to keep access leaves a permanent assignment, and this test lists it.

The test lists every active assignment to a privileged role. Users and groups pass when the assignment type is **Activated**. Service principals pass when the assignment has an end date. Permanent Global Administrator assignments are accepted only for accounts listed in the EmergencyAccessAccounts setting of …
tests.fix:
1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Go to **Entra ID** > **Roles & admins**, or open [Privileged Identity Management](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_PIMCommon/ResourceMenuBlade/~/roles/resourceId//resourceType/tenant/provider/aadroles) and select **Microsoft Entra roles**.
3. Open **Assignments** > **Active assignments** and select each permanent assignment of a privileged role.
4. Select **Update** and change the assignment to **Eligible**, then save.
5. Ask the administrators to activate their role when they need it. Keep two cloud-only emergency access accounts as the only permanent Global Administrators, and list them in the EmergencyAccessAccounts setting of maester-config.json.

links.t: Microsoft Entra admin center - Privileged Identity Management
Assign Microsoft Entra roles in Privileged Identity Management
Best practices for Microsoft Entra roles

tests.title: Ensure 'Access reviews' for guest users are configured
tests.sum:
A recurring access review of guest users exists, repeats at least monthly and applies its decisions automatically.

Guest accounts are created for a project and then forgotten. Each one keeps its access, and the external organisation that owns the identity can change or lose control of it without you noticing. A regular access review asks the owners to confirm that each guest still needs access, and removes those who are not confirmed.

The review must repeat weekly or monthly, give reviewers no more than 14 days, send notifications and reminders, ask for a justification when access is approved, apply results automatically, deny access when no one responds and have no end date. Access reviews need Microsoft Entra ID Governance or Microsoft Entra ID P2 licences.
tests.fix:
1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Go to **ID Governance** > [**Access reviews**](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_ERM/DashboardBlade/~/Controls/menuId/) and select **New access review**.
3. Select **Teams + Groups** and choose **All Microsoft 365 groups with guest users** (or a selected set of groups).
4. Under **Scope**, choose **Guest users only**.
5. Set the reviewers, a **Weekly** or **Monthly** recurrence, a duration of 14 days or less and **No end date**.
6. Under **Upon completion settings**, turn on **Auto apply results to resource** and set **If reviewers don't respond** to **Remove access**.
7. Under **Advanced settings**, turn on **Require reason on approval**, **Mail notifications** and **Reminders**, then create the review.

links.t: Microsoft Entra admin center - Access reviews
Create an access review of groups and applications in Microsoft Entra ID
Manage guest access with access reviews

tests.title: Ensure 'Access reviews' for privileged roles are configured
tests.sum:
The Global, Exchange, SharePoint, Teams, Security and Privileged Role Administrator roles each have a recurring access review that is configured as required.

Role assignments accumulate: people change jobs, projects end and temporary access becomes permanent. A recurring review makes the people who know the context confirm who still needs each privileged role, and removes the others.

Each of the six roles needs an active review that covers users and groups, repeats weekly or monthly, gives reviewers 14 days or less, sends notifications and reminders, asks for a justification when approving, applies results automatically, uses the default decision of **No change** and does not end. Access reviews need Microsoft Entra ID Governance or Microsoft Entra ID P2 licences.
tests.fix:
1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Go to **ID Governance** > **Privileged Identity Management** > **Microsoft Entra roles** > **Access reviews** and select **New**.
3. Select the review scope **Users and Groups**, add the role to review (for example Global Administrator) and choose the **Assignment type**.
4. Set the reviewers, a **Weekly** or **Monthly** recurrence, a duration of 14 days or less and **No end date**.
5. Under **Upon completion settings**, turn on **Auto apply results to resource** and set **If reviewers don't respond** to **No change**.
6. Under **Advanced settings**, turn on **Require reason on approval**, **Mail notifications** and **Reminders**, then start the review.
7. Repeat for the other roles in the list.

tests.title: Ensure approval is required for Global Administrator role activation
tests.sum:
Activating the Global Administrator role in Privileged Identity Management needs approval from at least one other person.

Global Administrator can change anything in the tenant. If an attacker gets an eligible account, MFA is the only barrier to activating the role. Requiring approval adds a second person who can refuse an activation that looks wrong, and creates a record of why it was granted. Without approval, an attacker with an eligible account can take temporary elevated access silently.

Approval slows urgent changes, so define more than one approver and agree how to handle out-of-hours requests. Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Microsoft Entra ID Governance licences are required.
tests.fix:
1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Go to [Privileged Identity Management](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_PIMCommon/ResourceMenuBlade/~/roles/resourceId//resourceType/tenant/provider/aadroles) > **Microsoft Entra roles** > **Roles** and select **Global Administrator**.
3. Select **Role settings** > **Edit**.
4. On the **Activation** tab, select **Require approval to activate** and **Select approvers**. Add at least one user or group.
5. Select **Update**.

links.t: Microsoft Entra admin center - Privileged Identity Management
Approve or deny requests for Microsoft Entra roles in PIM
Configure Microsoft Entra role settings in PIM

tests.title: Ensure approval is required for Privileged Role Administrator activation
tests.sum:
Activating the Privileged Role Administrator role in Privileged Identity Management needs approval from at least one other person.

Privileged Role Administrator can manage role assignments and PIM settings, which means that it can give itself, or anyone, any other role, and can weaken the approval requirements on other roles. Treating it like Global Administrator closes that route around the approval for other roles.

If an attacker gets an eligible account, MFA is the first barrier to activating the role. Approval adds a second person who can refuse an activation that looks wrong, so it is a layer behind MFA.

Approval slows urgent changes, so define more than one approver and agree how to handle out-of-hours requests. Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Microsoft Entra ID Governance licences are required.
tests.fix:
1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Go to [Privileged Identity Management](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_PIMCommon/ResourceMenuBlade/~/roles/resourceId//resourceType/tenant/provider/aadroles) > **Microsoft Entra roles** > **Roles** and select **Privileged Role Administrator**.
3. Select **Role settings** > **Edit**.
4. On the **Activation** tab, select **Require approval to activate** and **Select approvers**. Add at least one user or group.
5. Select **Update**.

tests.title: Ensure SharePoint and OneDrive integration with Azure AD B2B is enabled
tests.sum:
7.2.2 (L1) Ensure SharePoint and OneDrive integration with Azure AD B2B is enabled

Entra ID B2B provides authentication and management of guests. Authentication happens via one-time passcode when they don't already have a work or school account or a Microsoft account. Integration with SharePoint and OneDrive allows for more granular control of how guest user accounts are managed in the organization's AAD, unifying a similar guest experience already deployed in other Microsoft 365 services such as Teams.

>Note: Global Reader role currently can't access SharePoint using PowerShell.
tests.fix:
1. Connect to SharePoint Online using `Connect-SPOService`
2. Run the following command:

```powershell
Set-SPOTenant -EnableAzureADB2BIntegration $true
```

>Default Value: False

tests.title: Ensure external file sharing in Teams is enabled for only approved cloud storage services
tests.sum:
8.1.1 (L2) Ensure external file sharing in Teams is enabled for only approved cloud storage services

Microsoft Teams enables collaboration via file sharing. This file sharing is conducted within Teams, using SharePoint Online, by default; however, third-party cloud services are allowed as well.

>Note: Skype for business is deprecated as of July 31, 2021 although these settings may still be valid for a period of time. See the link in the references section for more information.
tests.fix:
To change third-party cloud services using the UI:

1. Navigate to **Microsoft Teams admin center** [https://admin.teams.microsoft.com](https://admin.teams.microsoft.com).
2. Select **Settings & policies > Global (Org-wide default) settings.**
3. Click **Teams** to open the **Teams settings** section.
4. Under files set storages providers to **Off** unless they have first been authorized by the organization.

To change third-party cloud services using PowerShell:

1. Connect to Teams using **Connect-MicrosoftTeams**.
2. Run the following PowerShell command to disable external providers that are not authorized. (the example disables Citrix Files, DropBox, Box, Google Drive and Egnyte)

```powershell
$Params = @{
 Identity = 'Global'
 AllowGoogleDrive = $false
 AllowShareFile = $false
 AllowBox = $false
 AllowDropBox = $false
 AllowEgnyte = $false
}
Set-CsTeamsClientConfiguration @Params
```

tests.title: Ensure communication with unmanaged Teams users is disabled
tests.sum:
8.2.2 (L1) Ensure communication with unmanaged Teams users is disabled

This policy setting controls chats and meetings with external unmanaged Teams users (those not managed by an organization, such as Microsoft Teams (free)).

The recommended state is: **People in my org can chat and have meetings with external users who have unmanaged Microsoft accounts set to Off**.
tests.fix:
To remediate using the UI:

1. Navigate to [Microsoft 365 Teams Admin Center](https://admin.teams.microsoft.com).
2. Click to expand **External collaboration** and select **External access**.
3. Select the **Policies** tab
4. Click on the **Global (Org-wide default)** policy.
5. Set **People in my org can chat and have meetings with external users who have unmanaged Microsoft accounts** to **Off**.
6. Click **Save**.

>Note: Configuring this setting at the organization level, in the **Organization settings** tab, to **Off** is also a compliant remediation.

links.t: IT Admins - Manage external meetings and chat with people and organizations using …
Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams
GIFShell Attack Lets Hackers Create Reverse Shell through Microsoft Teams GIFs
CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations Benchmark v7.0.0 - Page 512

tests.title: Ensure external Teams users cannot initiate conversations
tests.sum:
8.2.3 (L1) Ensure external Teams users cannot initiate conversations

This setting prevents external users who are not managed by an organization from initiating contact with users in the protected organization. The recommended state is to uncheck **External users with Teams accounts not managed by an organization can contact users in my organization**.

>Note: Disabling this setting is used as an additional stop gap for the previous setting which disables communication with unmanaged Teams users entirely. If an organization chooses to have an exception to (L1) Ensure communication with unmanaged Teams users is disabled they can do so while also disabling the ability for the same group of users to initiate contact. Disabling communication entirely will also disable the ability for unmanaged users to initiate contact.
tests.fix:
To remediate using the UI:

1. Navigate to [Microsoft 365 Teams Admin Center](https://admin.teams.microsoft.com).
2. Click to expand **Users** select **External access**.
3. Select the **Policies** tab
4. Click on the **Global (Org-wide default)** policy.
5. Locate the parent setting **People in my organization can communicate with unmanaged Teams accounts**.
6. Uncheck **External users with Teams accounts not managed by an organization can contact users in my organization**.
7. Click **Save**.

>Note: If People in my organization can communicate with unmanaged Teams accounts is already set to Off then this setting will not be visible and will satisfy the requirements of this recommendation.
